newsitem.title: USA: First Team Q4 hurt by inventories, prices.
newsitem.headline: First Team Q4 hurt by inventories, prices.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc, which makes in-line skates and roller hockey products, said its fourth quarter loss was due to significantly lower margins caused by excess retail inventories and competitive pricing.

Earlier it reported net sales for the fourth quarter ended February 28 of $13.6 million, compared to $21 million a year ago. It had a fourth quarter loss of $0.09 a share versus earnings of $0.23 a year ago.
Going into the spring selling season, bookings for the UltraWheels' new Softec line of high performance skates were strong worldwide, John Egart, president, said in a statement.
He added that First Team's Sabotage line of skates also were competing well in the aggressive skating market.

"We believe this early, strong acceptance of our spring skate line, combined with improved inventory levels at the specialty and sporting good chain stores, will give First Team the opportunity to take advantage of a potentially improved marketplace in these channels of distribution in fiscal 1998," Egart said. "While we have some basis for optimism, we remain cautious as to whether the improvement in the marketplace can sustain itself."
